items.title: Florida Atlantic coast flooded by record rainfall
items.feedTitle: Northeastern Florida now under flood threats from heavy rain that has devastated coastal communities
items.summary: Parts of Florida's east coast, particularly the Northeastern region, have been deluged with over 17 inches of rainfall since Tuesday, according to preliminary weather service totals. The severe flooding has devastated coastal communities and is expected to continue as storms move northward. Road closures and travel disruptions are ongoing across Central and Atlantic Florida as residents face threats from additional incoming rain.

items.title: White House names new cybersecurity director after outages
items.feedTitle: White House taps Kirsten Davies as cyber chief after outages rattle Americans
items.summary: The White House appointed Kirsten Davies as national cyber director Thursday, following widespread service outages that disrupted Americans' daily lives. The move comes after the previous cyber official lost confidence of White House leadership amid the telecom infrastructure failures. Davies's appointment signals an effort to address the nation's vulnerability to cyber threats.

items.title: Second federal judge blocks Trump's triumphal arch construction
items.feedTitle: A second judge blocks Trump's arch, saying it's unlikely to succeed in court
items.summary: A federal judge in Virginia issued a preliminary injunction against Trump's proposed 'triumphal arch' at Arlington National Cemetery, going further than a D.C. judge's earlier temporary block. The judge expressed skepticism about the project's legal viability, citing lack of congressional approval. The ruling reflects ongoing concerns from families of the fallen over the monument's appropriateness at the cemetery.

items.title: GOP senator blocks Trump cybersecurity nominee over Jan. 6
items.feedTitle: Tillis blocks Trump cybersecurity nominee who refused to acknowledge Jan. 6 attack
items.summary: Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) said he will not allow Trump's nominee for cybersecurity director to advance because the nominee refused to acknowledge the January 6, 2021 Capitol attack during a hearing. Tillis cited the nominee's unwillingness to recognize the event as disqualifying for a role overseeing critical infrastructure security. The hold represents a rare Republican pushback on Trump personnel decisions.

items.title: Senate passes bipartisan energy bill to speed approvals
items.feedTitle: Senate passes bipartisan energy bill amid environmental concerns
items.summary: The Senate passed a bipartisan bill aimed at speeding up approval processes for data centers and power plants amid rising energy demands driven by AI growth. The legislation seeks to lower energy costs for Americans by reducing approval timelines and limiting court challenges to energy projects. The bill reflects bipartisan concern over energy availability as technology companies expand infrastructure.

stlouis.title: MetroLink extension to airport begins service after Thanksgiving
stlouis.feedTitle: MetroLink extension to MidAmerica St. Louis Airport gets opening date
stlouis.summary: The MetroLink extension connecting to MidAmerica St. Louis Airport is set to open shortly after Thanksgiving, expanding transit access to the region's major airport. The project represents a significant infrastructure development for the St. Louis metro area, improving connectivity between the city and its transportation hub. Service is expected to begin in the coming weeks.

stlouis.title: Missouri S&T launches undergraduate AI degree program
stlouis.feedTitle: Missouri S&T aims for AI undergrad degree next fall
stlouis.summary: Missouri University of Science and Technology aims to launch an undergraduate degree in artificial intelligence next fall, adding to academic offerings in the technology field. The program reflects growing demand for AI-educated professionals in Missouri and the broader region. The initiative positions Missouri S&T as a leader in AI education in the Midwest.

stlouis.title: Two beloved St. Louis restaurants announce 2027 closures
stlouis.feedTitle: 2 Beloved St. Louis Area Restaurants Say They're Closing in 2027
stlouis.summary: Two popular St. Louis area restaurants have announced they will close in 2027, marking the end of their local operations. The closures reflect ongoing challenges in the food service industry as establishments reassess their viability. The announcements have drawn attention from the local community regarding changing dining landscape in the metro area.

items.title: US, Israel weigh renewed military strikes on Iran
items.feedTitle: U.S. and Israel considering new assault on Iran, sources say
items.summary: According to official sources, the U.S. and Israel are considering a new assault on Iran as Israeli officials press for action. The potential strikes come amid escalating regional tensions and ongoing concerns about Iran's military capabilities. U.S. officials are still weighing options as the administration considers its response to Iranian activities in the region.

items.title: UK, EU reach reset deal on trade, emissions, youth mobility
items.feedTitle: Burnham seals trade and youth mobility deals in biggest step towards EU since Brexit
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham reached agreements with the EU on food and drink trade, emissions trading, and a youth mobility scheme, marking the most significant step toward closer EU ties since Brexit. The deals aim to ease trade checks and create pathways for young people to move between the UK and continent. Negotiations on student fee arrangements remain unresolved and may complicate further progress.

items.title: Tanker catches fire after projectile strike near Hormuz
items.feedTitle: Tanker catches fire after projectile strike near Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says
items.summary: A tanker caught fire after being struck by a projectile near the Strait of Hormuz, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations. The incident adds to escalating tensions in one of the world's most critical shipping lanes. No immediate details on casualties or the source of the attack were provided, though the incident underscores maritime security concerns in the region.

items.title: European troops conduct postwar Ukraine deployment drill
items.feedTitle: European troops from 11 countries hold a drill in Poland for a potential postwar Ukraine mission
items.summary: Troops from eleven European countries held a military drill in Poland to prepare for potential postwar Ukraine operations. The exercise demonstrates NATO's preparedness for future peacekeeping or stabilization missions in Ukraine. The drill took place as diplomatic efforts continue regarding Ukraine's security guarantees and territorial integrity.

items.title: Indian man sentenced to 19 years for Pannun murder plot
items.feedTitle: U.S. court sentences Indian national Nikhil Gupta to 235 months in jail in Pannun murder plot
items.summary: An Indian national, Nikhil Gupta, was sentenced to over 19 years in U.S. prison for pleading guilty to orchestrating a failed government-backed plot to assassinate a Sikh separatist in New York. Gupta admitted to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire, and money laundering charges. The case highlights allegations of Indian government involvement in targeting dissidents abroad.

items.title: India takes note of Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit
items.feedTitle: India ‘takes note’ of Trump-Xi-Putin summit, awaits more details
items.summary: India stated it is taking note of the historic trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi Jinping, and Putin in China, while awaiting more details on outcomes. The summit produced a joint declaration on peace and pledges regarding oil supplies and nuclear weapons talks. India's cautious response reflects its diplomatic interest in the summit's implications for regional and global stability.

items.title: Cheetah born in Botswana gives birth to four cubs in India
items.feedTitle: Cheetah brought from Botswana gives birth to four healthy cubs, population now at 62
items.summary: A cheetah brought to India from Botswana has successfully given birth to four healthy cubs in the wild at Kuno National Park, raising India's cheetah population to 62. The birth represents a significant achievement in India's wildlife reintroduction program and conservation efforts. The successful reproduction demonstrates the viability of the breeding program and offers hope for the species' recovery in India.

items.title: PM Modi to inaugurate new Kolkata Metro stretch soon
items.feedTitle: New Garia to Sector V in 30 mins: PM Modi to launch Kolkata Metro stretch soon
items.summary: Prime Minister Modi is set to inaugurate the Beleghata-Sector V stretch of Kolkata Metro's Orange Line, which will reduce travel time from New Garia to Sector V to approximately 30 minutes. The new extension represents a major infrastructure development for Kolkata's public transportation system. The opening is expected by year-end and will enhance connectivity across the city.

items.title: India's core infrastructure output hits 10.9% in October
items.feedTitle: India's core infrastructure output hits new-series high of 10.9% in October
items.summary: India's core infrastructure output reached a new series high of 10.9% in October, reflecting strong economic momentum in key sectors. The growth surpasses previous records and suggests robust expansion in infrastructure development. The figure indicates positive momentum in construction, power, and industrial output across the economy.

immigration.title: DOL proposes sweeping PERM labor certification overhaul
immigration.feedTitle: Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the PERM Immigrant Visa Program
immigration.summary: The U.S. Department of Labor has proposed major changes to the PERM (Permanent) labor certification process, including stricter recruitment standards and a 90-day recruitment period with a 2-year layoff bar for companies sponsoring foreign workers. This marks the first significant PERM modernization in nearly 20 years and tightens protections for U.S. workers. The proposed rule is not yet final and subject to comment periods. The changes would substantially raise the bar for employers seeking to hire foreign workers on a permanent basis.

immigration.title: H-1B visa workers abandoning US tech jobs over delays
immigration.feedTitle: H-1B Visa Workers Are Fed Up and Abandoning American Tech Jobs
immigration.summary: H-1B visa workers are increasingly leaving the U.S. and American tech jobs due to processing delays and fees under Trump's immigration policies. Bloomberg reports that skilled tech workers are becoming frustrated with extended wait times and rising costs associated with the visa program. The trend suggests potential talent drain from the U.S. technology sector as workers explore alternatives abroad.

immigration.title: Bill proposes green card pathway for H-1B workers' children
immigration.feedTitle: H-1B visa workers' children could get Green Card pathway under this US Bill
immigration.summary: A proposed U.S. bill would create a pathway to permanent residency for children of H-1B visa workers, addressing long-standing concerns about family separation and visa backlogs. The legislation seeks to ease immigration procedures for families of skilled workers currently in the U.S. on temporary visas. The proposal is not yet enacted into law but reflects growing congressional interest in H-1B family issues.

items.title: S&P 500 enters correction amid AI trade unraveling
items.feedTitle: Stock Market Today: Dow, S&P 500 fall, Nasdaq wipes out 2026 gains as stocks head for worst week since 'liberation day'
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 10% from its recent record high and entered correction territory as investors reassess the AI trade. The Nasdaq wiped out all 2026 gains amid broad tech sector weakness, with semiconductor and AI stocks leading declines. Market analysts attribute the sell-off to concerns about massive investments in AI infrastructure and questioning whether returns will justify the spending, marking a significant shift in market sentiment.

items.title: Anthropic shares tumble after record IPO debut
items.feedTitle: Anthropic Shares Slip as AI and Tech Stock Sell-Off Continues
items.summary: Anthropic's shares fell sharply on its second day of trading after the AI company completed the largest IPO in history, raising $91 billion. Despite the blockbuster debut, investor enthusiasm waned quickly, with the stock retreating from opening gains. The disappointing post-debut performance has fueled broader concerns about the AI investment boom and whether mega-IPOs can sustain valuations.

items.title: Indian markets surge despite global tech sell-off
items.feedTitle: Markets Nov 20: Sensex gains 900 pts; Nifty closes above 25,800 while Bank Nifty scales fresh record high
items.summary: India's Sensex jumped 898 points and Nifty reclaimed the 25,800 mark, with Bank Nifty hitting an all-time high of 64,600. Indian banking stocks led the rally as foreign portfolio investor inflows supported markets. India's market performance contrasts sharply with global weakness, as rupee strength and cooling crude oil prices provide tailwinds for domestic equities.

items.title: AI fever in markets breaks as reality sets in
items.feedTitle: The AI fever in markets is breaking
items.summary: The Financial Times reports that the AI fever gripping markets is breaking, with investors reconsidering the economic case for massive AI infrastructure spending. Market analysts worry the AI trade may be nearing exhaustion as enthusiasm fades and questions mount about return on investment. The shift in sentiment marks a turning point after months of unbridled optimism about AI's commercial potential.

items.title: IMF warns AI demand will push interest rates higher
items.feedTitle: AI demand will push up interest rates around the world, IMF head warns
items.summary: The International Monetary Fund's chief, Kristalina Georgieva, warned that booming demand for artificial intelligence will force central banks around the world to raise interest rates. The IMF cautions that countries must be prepared for the economic implications of rapid AI technology rollout. Georgieva emphasized that policymakers cannot afford complacency in adapting to AI-driven economic changes.

finance.note: Oil prices have held relatively steady as Iran tests U.S. blockades with crude transfers, while U.S. stocks suffered their worst week since 2020 with the S&P 500 entering correction territory down 10% from records—the Nasdaq wiped out all 2026 gains as the AI trade unravels following Anthropic's disappointing post-IPO performance. Watch for upcoming Fed signals on rate paths, any escalation in Iran-Saudi tensions affecting crude, and earnings reports from mega-cap tech firms that might stabilize AI sector sentiment.

cards.title: Gather incomplete information fast
cards.insight: Markets and organizations move on partial data daily. Waiting for perfect clarity often means missing decision windows. The S&P 500 sell-off accelerated as investors questioned AI spending ROI—not because they had complete proof, but because doubt emerged faster than justification arrived.
cards.takeaway: Set decision thresholds in advance: define what 'enough information' looks like before you need it, so you act decisively rather than defensively when uncertainty rises.

cards.title: Reversals expose hidden assumptions
cards.insight: Trump's cybersecurity nominee and green-card rules reveal how leaders assume consensus exists where it doesn't. Sen. Tillis blocked the nominee not because the position was controversial, but because a core assumption—that Jan. 6 was settled—wasn't shared. Reversals in market sentiment (AI sell-off) often signal broken assumptions about economic fundamentals.
cards.takeaway: When a decision stalls or a trend reverses, ask: 'What assumption did I silently hold?' Write them down before they derail you.

cards.title: Decisions compound over time
cards.insight: India's cheetah reintroduction, the PERM labor certification overhaul, and Florida's MetroLink extension all show that slow incremental moves—breeding success, regulatory clarity, infrastructure delivery—compound into transformative outcomes. Quick reversals (H-1B freeze rollback proposals) often fail because they lack the foundation slow decisions build.
cards.takeaway: Distinguish urgent decisions from important ones. Invest early in foundational choices (hiring, standards, processes) even if payoff isn't immediate; they compound.

cards.title: Signals matter more than statements
cards.insight: Trump's offshore mining lease and data-center restrictions send messages—control of strategic resources and limits on tech abroad—that matter more than press releases. Similarly, Anthropic's stock tumble signals something markets believe despite the CEO's public confidence. Listen to what decisions reveal, not what words claim.
cards.takeaway: When evaluating a leader or organization, track *decisions made* over *words spoken*. Decisions reveal true priorities and beliefs faster than rhetoric.

ai.title: Anthropic IPO fails to revive faltering AI trade
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic IPO Didn’t Save the AI Trade
ai.summary: Anthropic's record-breaking $91 billion IPO could not stem the broader tech sell-off, with AI stocks tumbling across the board. The largest IPO ever completed did little to restore investor confidence in the AI sector, as concerns mount about the economics of AI infrastructure spending. The failed momentum marks a significant turning point for an industry that has enjoyed sustained investor enthusiasm.

ai.title: Anthropic mathematician claims AI solved Riemann hypothesis
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic Mathematician Says AI Has Solved the Most Famous Problem in Math
ai.summary: An Anthropic mathematician says Claude AI has solved the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics' most famous unsolved problems and a Clay Millennium Prize problem worth $1 million. If verified, the breakthrough would represent a landmark achievement in both mathematics and AI capabilities. The claim reflects the growing sophistication of large language models in tackling complex mathematical problems.

ai.title: US approved nearly 880,000 AI chips for Chinese buyers
ai.feedTitle: U.S. Cleared Nearly 880,000 AI Chips for Chinese Buyers
ai.summary: According to House records, the U.S. cleared nearly 880,000 Nvidia and AMD AI chips for Chinese companies, raising questions about technology transfer restrictions. The approvals suggest significant loopholes in export controls intended to limit China's access to advanced semiconductor technology. The scale of approved chip shipments may undermine stated U.S. policy objectives regarding AI technology and national security.

ai.title: SpaceX raises $32 billion for AI chip infrastructure
ai.feedTitle: SpaceX Just Raised $32 Billion for AI Chips. Lenders Want Elon Musk to Keep Them on Earth.
ai.summary: SpaceX secured $32 billion in debt financing specifically for AI chip infrastructure, with lenders reportedly seeking restrictions on deploying the chips into orbit. The massive funding round reflects confidence in AI's economic potential but also concerns about Elon Musk's plans for space-based compute. Lenders are imposing conditions to keep the AI chips on Earth rather than launching them into orbit.

ai.title: Trump opposes 'globalist' AI regulation during APEC
ai.feedTitle: Trump says he opposes 'globalist' AI regulation during APEC Summit
ai.summary: During the APEC summit, Trump said he opposes 'globalist' AI regulation, signaling his administration's preference for limited government oversight of artificial intelligence development. The statement reflects Trump's broader deregulatory stance and skepticism of international coordinated approaches to AI governance. The position may shape U.S. AI policy and its international dimensions going forward.
